correctness.rationale: Counting the abc triangles by deleted-edge incidences proves the ab lower bound. Equality forces exactly one deletion per triangle, only on largest-incidence sides. This gives the unique minimum or independent switches at A in the first two cases. In the balanced exact-one equations, two differing AB rows have a nonzero constant difference and hence are constant 0/1 rows; subtraction against either forces every AB row constant, AC complementary, BC zero. Column variation is the symmetric case. A constant AB matrix either is a pure side or leaves a C-split. Two families meet only at their common pure-side state. Within a family the batch cost is class size times Hamming distance. Across two balanced families the only overlap is on AB, of size (n−p)(n−q), so the cost n(p+q)−pq exceeds n for p,q≥1 and n≥2. This proves both sharp thresholds and that the cubes are glued solely at the specified corners. The antipodal corner distance is n, so leaving a cube cannot shorten its internal metric; for distinct cubes the two shortest routing options have lengths s and 3n−s, for s the sum of distances to their shared corner. All integers 0≤s≤2n are realized, giving diameter floor(3n/2). Independent exact-one branching and BFS gave balanced (count, diameter) (9,3), (21,4), (45,6), (93,7) at n=2,3,4,5; it also checked representative asymmetric cases.
residual_risks: Finite branching checks only selected hosts; the incidence and distance proof supplies all quantifiers. Batch moves require legal endpoints, not legal one-edge intermediates.
